locations: Freetown lowlands and floodplains (no neighbourhoods named)
rain_note: Heavy rain; on 15 July 2020 Freetown City Council warned of heavy rain forecast for three more days
summary: Flooding on 14 July 2020 displaced residents of low-lying and floodplain areas of Freetown (the Sierra Leone Telegraph described minor displacement), prompting a Freetown City Council flood warning the next day.
evidence: ACAPS (4 Aug 2020): flooding on 14 July 2020 "has displaced residents living in lowlands and floodplains"; needs "currently unclear".

summary: Flooding of the coastal slums of Portee and Rokupa in eastern Freetown left about 60 people homeless and one dead (figures from Politico-SL 2020 as cited in peer-reviewed studies; flood mechanism not specified).
evidence: "the flooding left about 60 people homeless and resulted in one fatality (Politico-SL, 2020)"

locations: low-lying areas of Freetown (no neighbourhoods named)
rain_note: Heavy rains during the week ending 30 July 2021
summary: During the week ending 30 July 2021 heavy rains flooded low-lying Freetown communities with water several feet deep, and many people lost their homes (exact day not given).
evidence: "Communities in low-lying areas of Freetown are once again at the receiving end of the heavy rains... many people have this week lost their homes, as floods reaching several feet destroy houses and livelihoods" (Sierra Leone Telegraph, 30 Jul 2021)

rain_note: Heavy downpour on 17 Aug; Caritas describes flooding from 14 to 17 Aug 2022; first of two heavy rain spells in two weeks
summary: A heavy downpour on 17 August 2022 flooded Culvert and Kroo Bay; Caritas Freetown said Culvert was worst hit in flooding between 14 and 17 August.
evidence: "Culvert and Kroo Bay were flooded after a heavy downpour on 17 August, 2022"; Caritas: Culvert "was the worst hit in the flooding from August 14 to 17"

rain_note: Torrential rain on Sunday 28 Aug (Caritas: flooding 27-28 Aug); second heavy spell in two weeks; major roads 'transformed to heavy flowing rivers'
summary: Torrential rain on Sunday 28 August 2022 caused flash floods and a mudslide at Looking Town (Kissy) that killed six; AFP/Red Cross counted 8 dead (79 injured, 4 missing), NDMA said 800+ were displaced in Colbert, and the Red Cross DREF counted 12,903 people (1,817 households) affected by the late-August floods.
evidence: "At least eight people have been killed and hundreds displaced" (AFP); Telegraph: "six, including a family of three, were killed after a mudslide destroyed two homes in an informal settlement" at Looking Town

summary: A storm with heavy rain on 9-10 May 2023 caused floods and mudslides in Freetown, killing at least 7 (six in a wall collapse at Cline Town, one in a mudslide at Moyeiba); NDMA reported flood damage at the Leone Oil facility in Kissy and the PWD Junction on Pademba Road flooded.
evidence: "At least 7 people have lost their lives after storms and heavy rain caused flooding and mudslides in parts of Freetown." (FloodList)

summary: NDMA's national disaster risk management policy records severe flooding in Freetown and other parts of the country from heavy rains in August 2023, affecting over 10,000 people nationally (day and Freetown-only figures not given).
evidence: NDMA policy: in August 2023 "heavy rains led to severe flooding in Freetown and other parts of the country, affecting over 10,000 people"

rain_note: Persistent rains in Freetown since 1 July 2024
summary: In early July 2024 (before NDMA's 8 July assessment) flooding affected 200 households in Congo Town, Kolloh Town and Gray Bush, and a slope collapse in Congo Town killed one person and brought down a house.
evidence: NDMA: flooding "affected 200 households in Congo Town, Kolloh Town, and Gray Bush"; "a slope collapse in Congo Town resulted in one death and the collapse of a house"

summary: Flooding hit Waterloo and other East End communities on 16-17 July 2024 after 59.2 mm of rain; a school fence collapsed on the Allen Town-Waterloo Highway and one woman was briefly hospitalised (NDMA/SLMet joint assessment on 17 July).
evidence: flooding "linked to a significant cumulative rainfall of 59.2mm recorded from July 16-17, 2024"

rain_note: 106 mm in 3 hours (09:00-12:00) at SLMet Tower Hill station on Saturday 20 July 2024; highest since rains began 1 July; several days of rain
summary: Extreme rain on Saturday 20 July 2024 (106 mm in three hours) flooded low-lying Freetown; during the same multi-day spell Connaught Hospital wards were submerged, and a five-storey building at SS Camp collapsed late on 21 July amid heavy rain (reports of 1-2 dead, several missing).
evidence: SLMet "recorded a cumulative rainfall of 106mm from 9:00am to 12:00 noon"; Telegraph (24 Jul): "The wards in Freetown's main hospital were submerged in water after several days of rain"

summary: Intense rain on 24 October 2024 caused severe flooding: a fence collapse at Upper Melon Street (Old Road) swept away two men (one found dead, one missing), a school and church compound flooded at Texaco Old Road, and eight mud-brick homes were destroyed at Lower Kuntolor, displacing 150+ people (30 households).
evidence: NDMA: at Lower Kuntolor "eight mud-brick homes were destroyed by runoff from hillside waterways, displacing more than 150 people across 30 households"

locations: New England Ville (54 Off Pratt Street)
rain_note: Heavy downpour on the evening of Wednesday 23 July 2025
summary: A heavy downpour on the evening of 23 July 2025 sent floodwater and mud from the hills through New England Ville, collapsing a compound fence and destroying a home; NDMA confirmed three dead and a one-year-old girl missing, and floodwater also halted the President's motorcade in central Freetown.
evidence: NDMA: "at approximately 6:00 PM, following a heavy downpour, a section of a compound fence collapsed due to the massive flow of floodwater and mud cascading from the surrounding hilltops"

summary: Heavy morning rain on 23 May 2026 made a blocked, waste-filled gutter overflow into homes and pathways at Susan's Bay; no casualties were immediately reported.
evidence: Sierraloaded: gutter overflowed into homes; "No casualties were immediately reported at the time of reporting."

time_of_day: overnight into the early hours of Monday 3 August (6-7 hours of rain)
rain_note: Nearly seven hours of heavy rain (Truth Media); about six consecutive hours of exceptionally heavy rainfall on the night of 3 August (IFRC)
summary: Six to seven hours of heavy rain on 3 August 2026 caused flash floods and slope collapses across Freetown: a wall collapse at Metchem killed a girl, her mother and grandmother, more than 300 homes flooded in Juba/Portor with two children missing, and IFRC counted 4 dead, 8,915 people (1,763 families) affected, 700+ houses damaged or flooded and 18 water sources contaminated (DREF MDRSL022).
evidence: In Juba "over 300 homes were 'completely flooded'" (NDMA via Sierra Leone Telegraph); IFRC: "4 confirmed fatalities, over 8,915 affected people, more than 700 damaged or flooded houses"
